title: Security posture discovery - Zenith Health
summary: Intro discovery focused on security posture for evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Key topics: SOC 2 / ISO 27001 scope, SSO/SAML and IdP integration, RBAC and least privilege, audit logging and retention, encryption at rest using KMS/HSM, data residency and retention policies. Customer leaned toward Dedicated or Private for PHI-sensitive workflows but open to hosted for non-PHI. Next steps: share SOC2 and ISO attestations, network diagram template, SSO SAML guide, proposed pilot scope and pricing.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
next_steps: Alex to send SOC2 and ISO 27001 attestations (by 2026-10-16)
Priya to share SAML integration guide and sample metadata (by 2026-10-18)
Customer to provide network diagram and list of SRE contacts for Dedicated/Private connectivity review (by 2026-10-20)
Schedule technical deep dive/POC scoping with infra team (w/c 2026-10-26)
Redwood to propose pilot pricing and SLA options (by 2026-10-19)
action_items: Alex Chen - Send SOC2 + ISO reports - 2026-10-16
Priya Nair - Share SAML IdP metadata and SSO playbook - 2026-10-18
Zenith (Omar) - Upload network diagram & list of subnets/VPC peering needs - 2026-10-20
Miguel Torres - Draft Dedicated capacity sizing and rough cost estimate - 2026-10-19
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hi everyone thanks for making time, uh this is Alex from Redwood, with Priya and Miguel. How's every one doing?
[00:12] Laura Kim: Good thanks, Laura here. We were excited to talk through the security posture. We support a lot of PHI so we need to be pretty prescriptive.
[00:22] Alex Chen: Absolutely, understood. Maybe before we dive could you give a quick overview of where Zenith's workloads live today and what you consider regulated?
[00:34] Omar Rahman: Sure, we run most services in GCP, some analytics in AWS. The patient-facing chat and notes pipeline processes PHI - that's the big blocker. Non-PHI telemetry and product features could go to hosted.
[00:47] Priya Nair: Got it, so mixed workload. For Redwood we typically discuss Hosted for non-sensitive, Dedicated for predictable capacity with isolation, and Private (VPC or on-prem) when AWS/VPC-only controls or compliance require customer managed networking.
[01:05] Nina Patel: Is your SOC2 scope covering hosted customers as well? We need to know what the attestation covers and whether logs/auditability is in scope.
[01:14] Alex Chen: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001; I'll share the reports. Important note: the scope differentiates platform and customer data processing - we'll send the exact carve-outs.
[01:26] Sam Ortiz: For Dedicated, what's the network topology? Do we get VPC peering or private link? We can't have data cross public internet for PHI.
[01:35] Miguel Torres: For Dedicated we offer VPC peering and private connectivity, and for Private deployments we can run a control plane in your VPC or an on-prem bundle. There was a small mismatch in an earlier doc where we said VPC peering but actually recommended private link for certain clouds - we'll clarify.
[01:50] Laura Kim: Ok, also SSO is mandatory, SAML or oidc is ok but must integrate with Okta. Can you support Just-in-Time provisioning and SCIM?
[02:01] Priya Nair: We support SAML and OIDC; SCIM provisioning for user sync is supported via SAML/SCIM connector. We'll send the SAML metadata and example IdP config. Note there are occasionally transcription labels that call it SAML 2.0 but it's SAML just FYI.
[02:18] Omar Rahman: About RBAC - we need fine-grained roles, ability to restrict model selection and route access, and separation between engineers and ops. Does Redwood provide auditable RBAC logs?
[02:29] Miguel Torres: Yes, role-based access control with default roles and custom roles. Every API call and console action is logged; logs can be exported to your SIEM (we support exporting to Splunk/Datadog via a push or S3 bucket delivery). There is a small delay depending on retention config.
[02:46] Nina Patel: Encryption - at rest and in transit - we need customer-managed keys for PHI. Is KMS/HSM integration available?
[02:55] Alex Chen: For Hosted, we currently offer platform-managed encryption keys by default; customer-managed KMS is available for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted customers with strict KMS requirements we have an add-on that supports CMEK in select regions - we'll include the matrix.
[03:12] Sam Ortiz: How about audit logs and retention policy? We may need 7 years for certain artifacts for legal/regulatory reasons.
[03:21] Priya Nair: Our default audit log retention is 90 days on the console; for enterprise we can export full audit logs to your S3/GCS with custom retention and lifecycle. Seven years is long but possible via archived buckets and your retention rules. We'll document the pipeline.
[03:38] Laura Kim: Data residency - do you offer region locking? Data needs to remain in our EU region for some customers.
[03:46] Miguel Torres: Yes we can pin deployments to regions. Hosted has region-specific endpoints, Dedicated can be provisioned in region, and Private obviously stays in your environment. We'll ask for the list of regulated regions so we can map available hosts.
[03:58] Omar Rahman: For telemetry and model metrics, do you sample or do you send tokens? We need to ensure no raw PHI is logged in application telemetry.
[04:08] Priya Nair: Redwood supports token-level redaction and prefix KV caching is configurable; we also have a data governance setting to scrub PII before logging. By default we do not persist input text for longer than the configured retention and we can disable certain telemetry for PHI workloads. However, there have been occasions where wording in older docs suggested we keep short-term traces; we'll make the language clearer.
[04:30] Laura Kim: Can we see an example network diagram and an SLA for Dedicated - uptime and latency targets? Also need a runbook for incident response and data breach notification timelines.
[04:40] Alex Chen: Yes we'll include the network diagram template and our SLA tiers. Standard Dedicated SLAs are 99.9% with escalation paths; Private is governed by the enterprise contract. For incident response we have 72-hour initial notification for high-severity, but we can negotiate contractual timelines.
[04:58] Omar Rahman: Any pentest or third-party vulnerability assessment reports available?
[05:05] Miguel Torres: We run annual pentests and vulnerability scans and provide executive summaries; full reports can be shared under NDA. We also push CVE notifications and advise on patch schedules.
[05:16] Nina Patel: Ok on compliance, can we map Redwood controls to our internal control framework? Meaning we need a tech control matrix mapping SOC2 controls to Redwood features.
[05:26] Priya Nair: Yes we can provide a controls mapping spreadsheet - it maps SOC 2 criteria, ISO clauses, and how Redwood satisfies them. We'll include where the responsibility is shared (RACI).
[05:36] Sam Ortiz: For the pilot/POC, what's the minimal scope we can do for PHI? We prefer to do a Dedicated pilot in our VPC to validate latency and encryption flows.
[05:46] Alex Chen: That makes sense. We can propose a 4-week pilot on Dedicated capacity with VPC peering, customer-managed KMS, and audit log export to your S3. We'll size based on expected qps and token volume; Priya or Miguel can follow up with sizing questions.
[05:58] Omar Rahman: Pricing and contract terms - any minimums for Dedicated?
[06:03] Miguel Torres: We have reserved capacity commitments; minimums depend on GPU type and region. For pilots we often do a time-boxed trial with a reduced commit to validate performance. We'll include options in the proposal.
[06:15] Laura Kim: Do you support legal terms like data processing agreements and standard SCCs for EU?
[06:21] Alex Chen: Yes we have a DPA and support SCCs where applicable; for Private deployments we can craft bespoke agreements.
[06:28] Nina Patel: One last Q - if we go Hosted for non-PHI paths, what controls ensure segregation so a misrouted request doesn't end up in the PHI pipeline?
[06:38] Priya Nair: We recommend strict tagging and route-based policies; requests for PHI workloads should be routed to Dedicated or Private endpoints with enforced policies. We also have model routing and policy enforcement at the edge. We'll share routing best practices.
[06:54] Alex Chen: Great, let's recap action items. We'll send SOC2/ISO, SAML metadata, network diagram template, pilot proposal and pricing. Any other asks?
[07:04] Laura Kim: Please add the controls mapping and an example incident response runbook.
[07:10] Alex Chen: Noted. Thanks everyone - we'll follow up and propose the next technical deep dive.
[07:16] Omar Rahman: Thanks.
[07:19] End of meeting (approx 48 minutes).
